- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots in next 5-7 days; apply downward correction by 1-2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates further decline; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth transitions by averaging 3-5 day sentiment-weighted forecast adjustments.
- In high-sentiment periods (e.g., 0.8–1.0), model often forecasts higher than true outcome; cap forecast at 1.2x recent high if sentiment >0.7.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 days after peak, price drops 5–10%), model often fails to correct; apply mean-reversion bias correction by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates near-term (first 10 days) if sentiment is volatile; reduce first 5 days by 0.3–0.7% per sentiment volatility unit.
